required_actions: Check the drive is APFS or Mac OS Extended (Journaled); not a Time Machine drive, SD card, USB flash drive or network location
Close Photos
In Finder open the Pictures folder in the home folder where Photos Library is stored
Drag Photos Library onto the external drive (critical)
Double-click the library in its new location to open it
Optionally move the old library from Pictures to the Trash and empty the Trash to free space (critical for the goal)
Keep the drive connected and on before opening Photos
reasons: The reply hands the whole job to a link ('following Apple's guide ... https://support.apple.com/en-us/108345'). None of the page's actions are written out. The user's goal is freeing space, and space is freed only after the old library is removed from the Mac, which is not mentioned. The warning that Photos makes a new empty library if the drive is not connected is also missing.
fix: Replace step 2 with the page's steps in plain words, one per step: (a) the drive should be formatted APFS or Mac OS Extended (Journaled); do not use a Time Machine drive, SD card or USB flash drive; (b) close Photos; (c) in Finder, open your Pictures folder; (d) drag Photos Library onto the external drive; (e) when it finishes, double-click the library on the drive to open it; (f) only after you have checked your photos opened from the drive, move the old Photos Library in Pictures to the Trash and choose Finder > Empty Trash to free the space (say this removes the copy on the Mac, not the copy on the drive). Add: keep the drive plugged in and on before you open Photos, or Photos starts a new empty library. Keep the Storage check as the last step. Keep the link as a 'more help' line.
